newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Siemens falls on poor first half.
newsitem.headline: India's Siemens falls on poor first half.

text.p: Shares of Siemens Ltd fell on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) as brokerages recommended a hold following the firm's first half loss, brokers said.
The share fell by 27.75 rupees to 316.0 or 8.07 percent on the BSE in late morning trade. On the National Stock Exchange, Siemens fell 17.80 rupeess to 335.0.
The firm, the Indian subsidiary of Germany's Siemens AG, had stunned the market last month by posting a loss of 239 million rupees for the six months ended September 1996.
The company had attributed the loss to its telecommunications division which was starved of orders.
Investment firm HG Asia said it recommended a hold on Siemens Ltd following the results.
Siemens had built telecom switching capacities in Calcutta, hoping to get orders from the government monopoly as well as new private operators.

"However, the private sector is yet to take off and the political problems in the first half year have taken their toll on the functioning of DoT (government's Department of Telecommunications)," HG Asia said in a "hold" recommendation.
